mutant.description: AC1's guard is the load-bearing assertion of the whole cell -- it is the one thing standing between a terraform plan and a proposal to DESTROY the live opal-data-harvest bucket, and it was tested by running it against BOTH states of the file rather than only the fixed one. The pre-patch working tree IS the mutant: s3.tf naming the deleted bucket opal-data-research, which is what HEAD actually carried.
mutant.expected: Against the unfixed file the criterion should print 'harvest 0 research 1' and send the worker down its STOP branch; against the patched file it should print 'harvest 1 research 0'. If the criterion could not tell the two apart it would certify a bucket-destroying plan as safe.
mutant.observed: FIRED. Unfixed: 'harvest 0 research 1' with the resource block showing bucket = "opal-data-research". Patched: 'harvest 1 research 0' with bucket = "opal-data-harvest". Corroborated downstream by an instrument the criterion does not use: the AC6 plan, taken after the fix, contains NO aws_s3_bucket.harvest address at all and 0 destroy-marks and 0 replace-marks -- so the guard demonstrably prevented the destroy it names.

determinism.method: The two criteria whose failure carries the cell's whole verdict were re-run rather than reported from one observation. AC5's six-import loop was executed TWICE in full (the order's allowed single retry), the second time with exit codes and the first Error line exposed instead of `tail -1`, which is what revealed that the empty tails were hiding a hard failure. `terraform state list` was read after each run. AC1 was run twice by construction (before and after the patch). The live-plane reads behind AC7/AC8 were taken AFTER all terraform failures, so they date the world at the end of the session, not the start.
determinism.observed: IDENTICAL ACROSS RUNS. AC5: 6 of 6 imports rc=1 both times, same error string every time; state-resources 16 / chatter 0 both before and after both runs. AC6: plan-rc=1 with the same error at ri2.plan.txt:384. The 404 behind them was confirmed independently of terraform (head-object 404 with a positive control on the sibling key in the same call), so the determinism is a property of the world and not of one instrument.

declared_exclusions.item: Building and uploading s3://opal-313476888478-lambda-artifacts/research/opal-amgt-scoped-api.zip, the missing artifact that blocks every terraform operation in this root
declared_exclusions.reason: OUT OF CELL AND EXPLICITLY DIRECTED AGAINST. It belongs to the mount (AMGT-rf-2 / the round-10 mount cell), and infra/aws/terraform/harvest/scoped-amgt-api.tf:40-47 records that the issuing seat 'ruled AC1 a SOURCE-plane criterion and directed that no world act be taken'. Uploading it would be a world act on another cell's surface against a recorded direction, and ri-2 s.4's refusal clause forbids satisfying a criterion 'by a route this order did not name'. Refused and filed as AMGT_RESAPP-Z-W17-S2 instead.

declared_exclusions.item: A -target'ed terraform import/plan/apply that would route around the failing sibling data source
declared_exclusions.reason: AC6 and AC7 name an UNTARGETED whole-root plan and the apply of that exact plan file. A targeted plan is a different artifact with a different blast radius than the one the never-widen co-sign covers, and inventing it is precisely the 'repaired, widened or satisfied by a route this order did not name' the refusal clause bars.

declared_exclusions.item: Any alert, alarm, SNS topic, SES send, freshness checker, log subscription or monitor
declared_exclusions.reason: Standing moratorium, restated as a BOUND by this order. None was added. The only schedule touched is the pre-existing daily EventBridge Scheduler entry, which is a PRODUCER trigger and not a monitor.

declared_exclusions.item: Renaming the Lambda function, touching any DynamoDB table, or removing anything from any terraform state
declared_exclusions.reason: Forbidden by the order's BOUND (function_name is ForceNew, so a rename is a destroy). No table was touched; no `state rm` was run against any state. The stale amgt-resapp/tfstate and amgt-resapp/rd-2-security-metrics/tfstate objects remain in S3, inert, as the CRO's clean-up under C-S49.

declared_exclusions.item: org/critical_paths/.open_deploys/ sentinel and the deploy-completion entry
declared_exclusions.reason: Not created. The ledger's activation leg is the apply, which was refused before any world act; an entry opened against an act that never runs is itself the half-landed-deploy condition the ledger exists to detect.
